additionalCoursework:
Vanderbilt University School of Medicine recognizes that the undergraduate academic experience of applicants varies greatly. Therefore, we have made the decision to move away from “requirements” to “recommendations.” The expansive and ever-changing landscape of medicine and its practice necessitates that an applicant have demonstrated competencies in the natural and life sciences, social sciences, and mathematics. These competencies can be met through traditional and/or newly-established interdisciplinary courses of study in an accredited institution of higher learning. The use of AP or other credit is acceptable, but it is strongly encouraged to build stronger competencies through courses taken in college. Although there is no timeframe in which students must meet the above competencies, it is recommended that students have recent exposures to most or all of these areas. 
Please visit https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/md-admissions/admission-requirements/ for more information.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: As of 2-28-2025, there are numerous programs to support all students contributing to the diversity of our student body at Vanderbilt University School of Medicine, including the Student National Medical Association, Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association, Methuselah Society (non-trad students), 1GMD (first gen.), Pride in Medicine, and Latino Medical Student Association, to name a few. The Program for LGBTI Health is housed in VUMC ( https://www.vumc.org/lgbtq/ ).
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be granted by the Associate Dean for Medical Student Affairs for a period not to exceed one year for purposes of approved studies, recuperation from illness, or other special circumstances. Should it be necessary for a student to be absent for a period of more than one calendar year, the student must request approval from the Associate Dean for Medical Affairs for each year thereafter. If a student requests a leave while on probation, approval by the Promotions Committee is required both for the leave and the re-entry.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The richness of student life at the Vanderbilt School of Medicine is one of the many reasons students choose to pursue their medical training here. Currently, there are over sixty different organizations focused on the arts, advocacy, technology, wellness, community, politics, international affairs, and service. One can easily find numerous ways to get involved and be active while in Nashville. Additionally, student life is also influenced by the presence of the Vanderbilt Medical School Colleges Program. Each student is placed in one of the four colleges, allowing students to build a sense of community with other students from all years of training. The colleges are heavily invested in promoting student well-being through wellness initiatives; they also play an important role in our career counseling program. More recently, the colleges have blossomed into learning communities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Medical School is part of a 323-acre university campus that also serves as a national arboretum.  The location allows the medical students the opportunity to take advantage of programming that comes to the larger campus, including concerts, guest speakers, and sporting events, to name a few.  In addition, the location is convenient for the medical students who wish to do a joint degree program.  Vanderbilt is located about two miles from downtown Nashville, in the West End area.  Nashville has recently received a number of accolades about being an attractive city to live in, due to the friendliness of the citizens, weather, and economy; the city is very dynamic and has something for everyone.  We encourage you to visit to see for yourself!
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
There is no on-campus housing. A one bedroom apartment in Nashville rents on average of $1700 per month. Many of our students elect to live with roommates to lower costs (share the cost of utilities, etc.)  When students are admitted to the medical school, current students share resources on places to live and help with the transition to Nashville.  
Some of our students elect to live a bit further away from campus.  Our students are able to ride the city buses for free, by using their student id cards.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Vanderbilt University School of Medicine prides itself on having a robust Pride in Medicine student organization.  The group aids in orientation activities to ensure matriculating students are aware of support services available on campus and in the community.  Our LGBTQ+ students participate in admissions activities to encourage prospective students to become engaged in our vibrant community here.  Many LGBTQ+ students apply to Vanderbilt because of our Program in LGBTQ Health ( https://www.vanderbilthealth.com/lgbtqhealthprogram/ ).  Some of our applicants come to us through the LGBTQ Health Internship.  Our students find Vanderbilt and Nashville to be a supportive place for LGBTQ+ students.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Wellness is the cornerstone of the VUSM student experience.  Our comprehensive Student Wellness Committee focuses on mind, body, social, mentoring, education and research, and sustainability and community.  Leaders for these areas are selected by their peers.
The College System is another resource for our students.  Every college is lead by faculty members who serve as mentors, advocates, resources, guides, and networkers.  In the college, each student has a "Big Sib" who is a year ahead of the student.  The Big Sib also helps connect the student with resources to help them thrive.
Because we are all on the same campus, VUSM students are able to use the University Counseling Center ( https://www.vanderbilt.edu/ucc/ ) and other university resources such as our Student Rec Center https://www.vanderbilt.edu/recreationandwellnesscenter/ ) and Student Health Center ( https://www.vumc.org/student-health/welcome ).  There are also counselors dedicated to serving as mental health providers to our students.
Our administration, faculty, and staff provide a safe and supportive environment for our students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: It is a challenge to encapsulate the culture of VUSM in a small section.  If we had to boil the culture down to a sentence it is "Good people wanting to do good in the world."  Our students come from all walks of life and have unique life experiences (part of our holistic review in admissions).  On interview day, we make it clear:  if you are looking for a medical school where you can be anonymous and not leave your mark, PLEASE do not come to Vanderbilt.  Our faculty and leadership look out for our students.  If we do not see you in class, we will reach out to you.  Our classes are very engaging; we don't put you in a lecture hall all day because we are looking for your insight on topics.  We want you to take part in school activities, be it organizations or committees, because you matter.  Your experiences and thoughts help shape Vanderbilt for the better.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: During their School of Medicine careers, students may be placed for educational experiences in sites located a distance from the Vanderbilt University campus. Students are responsible for their own transportation to and from all sites for educational experiences, including all costs associated with that travel. For our students without cars, they either live with roommates who drive, or take advantage of our ample ride-share or car rental programs.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Since students are engaged in the clinical workplace throughout all years, the dress code requirements for clinical duties align with those of the medical center.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutoring is available for students who are struggling academically or who are deemed by the module director(s) and the Student Assistance Directors to be at risk for marginal performance.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are placed into a clinic at the beginning of year one and attend on a weekly basis. Supported by training sessions and seminars, students actively contribute to the care of patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: During the first 13 months, the instruction is mainly Case Based Learning, supplemented with Team Based Learning and some small lectures.  After the clinical year, years 3 and 4 are small group.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The second year provides clerkships in medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, psychiatry, and neurology. There are elective opportunities as well.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: There is no formal program before the start of orientation.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: The first two phases (years 1 and 2) are pass/fail.  The last two years are honors/high pass/pass/fail.   The class is not ranked, nor placed in quartiles.  Vanderbilt does not participate in AOA.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Most large group lectures are optional unless specifically designated as mandatory by the course director (for example, if a patient will be present). Small group team activities are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Curriculum 2.0 creates a responsive, agile system of life-long learning that: embraces innovation and improvement; fully integrates learning with patient care; rapidly translates discovery into practice; supports the professional growth of learners and teachers; creates physician leaders. 
In the first 13-months, course work in the basic sciences prepare students for the foundational clerkships. Blocks created around organ systems integrate normal and abnormal. Students will have a continuity clinic  to learn some of the soft skills of medicine.  In addition, students will have a weekly physical diagnosis experience for them to work with patients dealing with those health issues.
The next 10-month phase includes core clerkships, along with some elective opportunities to learn more about the various areas of medicine.
The last two years are Immersion courses that will solidify clinical skills; deepen foundational science knowledge through meaningful clinical engagement; allow students to dive into areas of personal learning needs and/or interest; expand knowledge and skills in leadership and scholarship; ensure readiness for residency; and enhance workplace learning skills. A three to six month research phase is a part of this phase.  During the Immersion Phase, each class is a month long.  This structure allows students to have more control over their academic and personal experience.
With the first two years being pass/fail and the last two years being Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail, students are graded against the competencies and not each other.  The class is not ranked, which allows for a more collaborative experience among students.

medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Vanderbilt requires Primary Care experiences of all medical students. Adult and pediatric experiences are available in community health and academic settings.   In addition, nearly all of our students volunteer at the Shade Tree  Clinic, a student-run free clinic meeting the needs of an underserved patient population of Nashville.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The involvement of medical professionals in the biomedical research enterprise is invaluable due to their position of direct access to patients, evidence-based knowledge of diseases and therapeutics and perspective regarding health systems and the policies that govern. Research education, training and experience is integrated throughout the medical school curriculum in order to cultivate physicians with the knowledge and skill base critical to the clinical practice of medicine, the conduct of biomedical research, and leadership in any arena of medicine. During the Inquiry Program, students participate in research-focused coursework and training in the first two years, and a 1-month project-planning course followed by 3 to 6 months of full-time mentored research during years 3 and/or 4. Students may elect to research in six broad areas: bench, bedside, bioinformatics, community and global health, epidemiology, and ethics, education, policy and society.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Foundations of Medical Knowledge last the first 13 months.  The Foundations of Clinical Care is 10 months.  The Immersion phase lasts 20 months and has a 3-6 month research phase built into it.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Although it is not required, many of our students partake in community service.  The Shade Tree Clinic is one opportunity for service.  This student-run clinic has a patient panel of 300 patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research can be in a variety of areas.  Please visit https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/md/curriculum/research/  for more information.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Students have the opportunity to gain exposures in a variety of clinical settings, from a large trauma 1 hospital to regional clinics.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: The first two phases (Foundations of Medical Knowledge and  Foundations of Clinical Care) are pass/fail.  Most courses in the Immersion Phase are graded as Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: The primary language of instruction is English, but opportunities exist for our students to practice medical Spanish through clinical opportunities.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Vanderbilt University School of Medicine is a private medical school located on the campus of Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee. The Medical Center (VUMC) is a 1,700+ bed general medical and surgical facility and is ranked nationally in 10 adult specialties.   VUMC is the largest transplant center in the nation and is one of the only burn unit in the state.  The Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt is a 363 bed facility with 10 out of 10 specialties nationally ranked.  In addition, the Vanderbilt Health Affiliated Network allows Vanderbilt to work with area health centers in the state and region to take patient care and population health to the next level.  Vanderbilt is the 5th largest recipient of funding from the NIH.  In addition, Vanderbilt  is home to the nation's largest health system DNA bio bank and the largest biomedical informatics department.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The School of Medicine is led by a talented and expert team of administrators, staff and faculty who are committed to the success of its people and the advancement of safe, effective, ethical, evidence-based, and patient-centered health care. 

The core values of Vanderbilt University School of Medicine are integrity, belonging, humility, fairness, mutual respect, and excellence.

Our Mission
The mission of Vanderbilt University School of Medicine is to catalyze the advancement of impactful discovery, servant leadership, and lifelong learning.

To carry out this mission, we make these strategic commitments:

*To nurture the growth of clinicians, scientists, and educators who will serve and lead their local, national, and global communities.
*To create, implement, and disseminate new knowledge that expands understanding of health, disease, and healthcare systems.
*To teach, learn, and provide compassionate, personalized caring of the highest quality for every patient who seeks our service and to strive to achieve health for all in the populations we serve. 
*To embrace a culture of lifelong learning, critical thinking, and innovation so that we will continuously improve in all we do.
*To build a broad community of faculty, staff, and students that expands the richness of our learning environment and enhances excellence in all of our endeavors.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes.  After a student has been accepted, VUSM will access the CBC from the AAMC.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks from receipt of acceptance letter.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Vanderbilt puts a great deal of weight on informative letters of evaluation.  We encourage candidates to work hard at developing relationships with individuals during their pre-med years with the hopes that the candidate will be able to collect strong letters of support for medical school.  The focus should be on relationship building, not necessarily just "getting letters."  The admissions committee enjoys reading letters that work together to paint a broad portrait of the candidate, instead of generic letters all from one area of the candidate's background.
Vanderbilt will distribute secondaries without letters of evaluation, but candidates will not be reviewed for an interview until letters of evaluation have been received.
MD/PhD candidates will definitely want letters from people who can address their abilities for that program.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Vanderbilt understands that everyone's journey to medical school is different; therefore, we do not have any requirements for letters.  If your school offers an advisor or committee letter, we will expect to receive a letter from that service.  We support the movement for letters to cover the competencies in the AAMC Guidelines ( https://students-residents.aamc.org/system/files/2023-11/23-144_Guidelines_for_Writing_a_Letter_of_Evaluation_One_Pager_Update_R1-1.pdf ) and encourage applicants to solicit letters from evaluators who can address competencies. If you have advanced degrees or at least one year of postgraduate full-time employment, it is advisable to ask your supervisor at work or a member of the graduate faculty to send a letter of recommendation.  We recommend a letter from your principle investigator, if you have done research.  Vanderbilt does not require a letter from a medical professional.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: For the 2026 cycle, Vanderbilt will conduct virtual interviews.  Candidates are invited to an informal gathering with current students virtually.  For the virtual interview day, VUSM utilizes a Zoom platform. For an hour before the interview, there is an informal conversation with a faculty member.  After the candidates interview, a session on the curriculum is held.  While interviewees are eating lunch, there is a student experience panel (no faculty or staff allowed).  After that session is over, VUSM explains the admissions and financial aid process.  There are also sessions throughout the cycle for interviewees to learn more about research.  Interviewees are encouraged to reach out with any questions they might have about the area or school.  The MD Ambassadors (https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/md/admissions/ambassadors/) are a wonderful way to get a current student's perspective.  The MD/PhD interview allows candidates to interview with potential research mentors.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invitations to interview for both the MD  and MD/PhD programs are sent via email from August until January.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two interviews are held.One interview is an open file (AMCAS and secondary) interview that lasts roughly 35 minutes.The other is a short, closed file interview that lasts roughly 20 minutes.Candidates spend the rest of the day learning more about us.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: VUSM will conduct Zoom interviews for this cycle.  Emails regarding additional information sessions for candidates will be sent to interviewees as the cycle progresses.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Selected applicants are invited to fill out the secondary application, after review of the verified AMCAS. Approximately 5700, out of over 7400 applicants, received secondaries for the 2026 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Because rolling admissions plays an important part in the process, we encourage candidates to submit the secondary around two weeks after receipt.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Tuition is the same for in and out of state students.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: As of 3-3-2026, there are no restrictions to be accepted to VUSM as an out of state applicant.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: We accept applications from any applicant who meets our academic and other prerequisites, without regard to citizenship or immigration status.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: We accept applications from any applicant who meets our academic and other prerequisites, without regard to citizenship or immigration status.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
ADMISSIONS PROCESS
Vanderbilt only receives verified AMCAS applications, which can take 4-6 weeks from AMCAS.  Once received, our committee ensures there is a current MCAT score and then screens to decide to give a secondary application.  Once the secondary and letters of evaluations are received, our Interview Review Subcommittee reviews to help determine an interview.  We interview on Mondays and Fridays from September to February.  After the interview, our Admissions Committee determines who will join the class.  We have a December and February wave of admissions; afterwards, candidates not admitted are placed on the waitlist.  Vanderbilt's goal is to utilize the waitlist to craft a class that reflects the mission of the school.  In the spring, admitted candidates attend Second Look Weekend, which provides these individuals the opportunity to learn more about Nashville and Vanderbilt.  Admitted students have a checklist that they can use to stay on track about immunizations, matriculation surveys, and other items.  As a reminder, admissions is contingent on a successful criminal background check, compliance with our technical standards and honor code along with the State of Tennessee immunization requirements, and documentation of graduation from an accredited institution.  Internationally educated candidates can find the following website helpful: https://registrar.vanderbilt.edu/academic-records/international-degrees.php .  Candidates are strongly encouraged to reach out to Admissions to clarify any questions they may have.

VANDERBILT SELECTION PROCESS
Vanderbilt looks at strong academic performance to help assure the ability to be successful in the curriculum.  Although there are no extracurricular requirements, it is recommended to have medical exposures, community engagement, leadership, and research experience before applying.  In addition, candidates who are successful typically have either a unique life experience or extracurricular activities that add unique experiences to the class.  No one activity to weighed more than the other.  Vanderbilt loves to see a strong interest in an activity, instead of using extracurriculars as a checklist for admissions.

Having a passion for medicine being evident in the application materials, along with strong letters of support are additional elements Vanderbilt evaluates in the holistic admissions process.

For the MD/PhD candidates, the selection process is typically the same. Candidates are encouraged to have strong letters of support for their ability to complete an MD/PhD.  The candidates usually have strong research skills.  Many candidates have a transition year after graduating college where they work full time in a research lab.  Quite a few candidates have been published or done presentations on their research.

REAPPLICANTS
Vanderbilt does not have a policy against reapplicants, but encourage candidates take time to personally evaluate their application materials.  When doing that, many candidates will work on areas of improvement and then reapply later.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Vanderbilt does not give any particular weight on the MCAT score; it is one piece of the entire application.  The admissions committee values the MCAT as it is a way to achieve a level view of applicants who had different educational journeys and majors before applying to medical school.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Although Vanderbilt does not a minimum MCAT, we encourage candidates to have at least a 70th percentile on the MCAT.  VUSM uses the MCAT and academic profile together to determine the ability to be successful in the curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: VUSM looks at the entire academic profile and not just a singular "GPA" when determining fit for the curriculum. Although Vanderbilt does not a minimum GPA, we encourage candidates to have at least a 3.0 GPA.  VUSM uses the academic profile and MCAT together to determine the ability to be successful in the curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Vanderbilt doesn't have a minimum GPA, but instead looks at performance trends in the classroom.  If the undergraduate coursework isn't strong, we encourage additional science courses for our committee to have confidence in the candidate's ability to be successful in the curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: It depends on the candidate's situation, but typically candidates who do additional science classes to increase their academic performance will have a minimum of 24 semester hours (or completion of a pre-med post-bac program).  We view all of our candidates as individuals, so it's hard to give one specific answer to this question.  We encourage candidates to work with their pre-med advisor at their college for additional advice.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Vanderbilt recognizes that everyone's pathway to medical school is different.  That is what sparked our movement from pre-requisites to recommendations.  Vanderbilt has no issue with candidates who take coursework at a community college, as long as their MCAT performance is strong.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Candidates who receive a secondary are invited to update their file, through our Admissions Portal.  
For interviewees, candidates are welcome to update their file with a Letter of Interest and explain why they feel a connection with VUSM.
For candidates on our waitlist, we encourage them to send a Letter of Intent as close to April 30th as possible.  VUSM considers a Letter of Intent to contain more specific interest about why they would like to matriculate.  The Admissions Office sends emails to waitlisted candidates to update them on the the admissions process.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Candidates must attest that they read the Technical Standards when they submit the secondary.  Any questions can be brought to the Director of Admissions.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Every effort is made to see that each medical student that qualifies for financial aid has sufficient funds to meet the total estimated cost of attendance by utilizing a variety of loans and scholarships. A fair proportion of the class receives a merit scholarship or funding through the Medical Scientist Training Program.  For the regular MD merit scholarship program, there are full tuition scholarships and partial tuition scholarships that are renewable for all four years towards successful completion of the MD degree.  Candidates do not have to do anything additional to apply for the merit scholarships.   There are need-based scholarships available, too.  Counseling is done to ensure the student understands the medical school financial aid process and debt management.  In addition, VUSM hosts several workshops throughout the year to  assist students with debt management and other issues related to budgets.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition will not go over 5% increase per year.

medSchoolSpecialty.specialtyTrainingTxt: Our students start career exploration as an M1, due to our engaging Careers in Medicine program.  With our students gaining medical exposures starting their M1, they are able to challenge themselves as to where they want to be in medicine.  There is a great deal of mentorship at VUSM, between the current students, residents, physicians, and administration.

medSchoolMatDemo.postbaccStudents: We accept students from both career changing and academic record enhancer post baccalaureate programs.  We also accept students who took advanced coursework outside of a formal program.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Vanderbilt University School of Medicine has several dual degree programs. For all dual degrees, except the MD/PhD, typically the first three years are spent in the medical school program. In most cases, after year three, students begin work on their other degree program. Depending on the other program, students may complete the second degree before returning to the medical school. The dual degree program allows students to reduce the period of time required to complete each degree separately, usually eliminating one full year of study. Application is made to each program separately, and admission to both programs is required to enter a dual degree program.


Please visit https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/md/opportunities/ to learn more about our various combined degrees, including ones not listed here.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Vanderbilt University School of Medicine Master of Public Health
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: Due to the collaborative nature of the VUSM curriculum, adding the MPH typically adds one year to the degree.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Because VUSM recognizes that candidates might not have been exposed to public health before matriculation, candidates apply for the dual degree during their time at Vanderbilt.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The MD curriculum allows students to customize their experience.  In the Medical Innovators Development Program (MIDP) our students enjoy an innovation-centered curriculum where they are empowered to solve the big problems in medicine (https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/midp/).   For students electing not to participate in MIDP, there are still opportunities to learn about medical designs and entrepreneurship.  Admitted students will be made aware of how to apply for the MIDP.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: The AAMC Plan to Enroll Date (PTE) becomes active in the AAMC Choose Your Medical School (CYMS) tool.

By April 30, 2026, admitted candidates must withdraw from all but one school. If the candidate intends to attend Vanderbilt, he/she/they must indicate “Plan to Enroll” in the “Choose Your Medical School” tool by midnight Central Time on April 30, 2026. Vanderbilt reserves the right to contact an admitted candidate if the individual is not compliant with this protocol.

Applicants are expected to follow both Vanderbilt and AAMC Applicant Protocols. Admissions will send emails to admitted students to notify and remind them of the action dates.  The Commit to Enroll date for MSTP is typically the fourth Friday in May.  For MD, it is typically the fourth Monday in June. Candidates who plan to attend VUSM are encouraged to stay in touch with admissions.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: All applicants not initially admitted will be placed on the non-ranked waitlist.  The number of candidates admitted ranges from around 0-20 each cycle.  VUSM accepts updates and letters of intent.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are encouraged to stay in touch with VUSM, as we view that as interest in staying on the non-ranked waitlist.  The committee uses a holistic review in selecting from the waitlist.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Vanderbilt University School of Medicine recognizes that the undergraduate academic experience of applicants varies greatly. Therefore, we have made the decision to move away from "requirements" to "recommendations". The expansive and ever-changing landscape of medicine and its practice necessitates that an applicant have demonstrated competencies in the natural and life sciences, social sciences, and mathematics. These competencies can be met through traditional and/or newly-established interdisciplinary courses of study in an accredited institution of higher learning. The use of AP or other credit is acceptable, but it is strongly encouraged to build stronger competencies through courses taken in college. Although there is no timeframe in which students must meet the above competencies, it is recommended that students have recent exposures to most or all of these areas. https://medschool.vanderbilt.edu/md/admissions/ .
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Vanderbilt does not have "prerequisites" and encourages candidates to take courses that will help prepare them for the MCAT and medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are reviewed without regard to race, sex, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, or state/country of residence. Applicants must agree to our Technical Standards ( https://www.vanderbilt.edu/catalogs/kuali/som-25-26.php#/home ).  There is a holistic review of academic performance and non-academic factors. For the 2026 cycle, approximately, 5700 candidates received a secondary, out of 7400 applicants. All MD/PhD candidates receive a secondary; for MD candidates, the verified AMCAS and MCAT scores are used to determine a secondary. Preparation for medical studies, motivation, personal qualities, letters of evaluation, and educational background are evaluated by a subcommittee to determine an interview; the Interview Review Subcommittee selected around 600 MD to interview for the 2026 cycle. The Admissions Committee reviews the AMCAS, secondary, letters, and interview reports to select the class.  The entire admissions process is mission aligned.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Vanderbilt does not have a mandatory requirement of shadowing doctors for admissions purposes; we recognize how difficult it can be to "shadow".  Our admitted students have a variety of exposures from working as a scribe, to shadowing doctors, to volunteering in a nursing home. The admissions committee wants to make sure the candidate can discuss motivations for a career in medicine; typically, the candidate had medical exposures to help the individual communicate the motivation.  Vanderbilt does NOT require a letter of evaluation be written by a doctor.  Due to the challenge of gaining in-person exposures, Vanderbilt encourages candidates to be creative in how they challenge themselves to display a passion for this career choice.
